Fourteen artifacts are byte-identical to evidence/.previous/, and the single artifact labelled "changed" is not: 08_state_propagating.mp4 is 5,380,163 bytes in both directories and every one of its 395 decoded frames has the same framemd5 as its counterpart, which I also confirmed pixel-for-pixel on ten full-resolution frames sampled every 40. what_is_working: One log, measured: all five region reports (01_pulse, 02_chat, 03_us, 04_moments, 05_settings) carry the identical "events": 14062 and "seed": 20260903, and each names its region as a view field rather than as a store of its own.

Partner state is legible on every region, not only Pulse: the ambient standing-line banner at x=60..1300, y=40..200 is pixel-identical (mean absolute difference 0.000, zero pixels differing by more than 10) across 01_pulse, 02_chat, 03_us, 04_moments, 05_settings, 12_search and 13_messenger_states.

Every module writes into the chat timeline. 11_chat_scroll carries, in one stream, text notes, a photograph (frame 133), feeling objects ("goodnight" crane at frame 76, "miss you" at 95, "long day" at 114, "a squeeze" at 190), Pulse signal dividers ("noor went out", "noor's phone is on silent", "you got in"), and a to-do event from the Us module ("text when home | KEPT · Sun 26 Apr · 07:20" at frame 152).

The same event is the same event in two regions: 01_pulse.report.json lists empty_chair from teo at ts 1788455973000, and 13_messenger_states.png shows that drawing in the chat stream as "empty chair · Thu 3 Sep · 17:19 read ✓✓", with the identical timestamp on the Pulse shelf.

Search is one search over the one log, not per-module search: evidence/logs/reliability.json records hits across nine types — message, photo, todo_event, date_event, feeling, state_declared, milestone, video, voice_note — and 12_search.png shows a message, a photograph, a to-do ("text when home · kept ... found in its note: rain the whole way") and video results interleaved under one query.

The fifth-module test is already answered on screen. 03_us.report.json lists five modules — dates (81 events), todos (199), calendar (6), rituals (53), shelf (12) — each with the same {id, events, glance} shape, and 03_us.png renders DATES and TO DO with the identical header-card-then-section pattern, so "shelf" is visibly a module added in the shape of the other four rather than a special case.

A feeling arrives wherever you are, not only on Pulse: 15_authored_feeling.mp4 frames 209–303 show the authored "pigeon" object landing while the Settings region is on screen, and 08_state_propagating.mp4 shows a Pulse state edit (mood "restless") reappearing as the "noor is restless" divider in Chat at frame 200.

The visual language survives a change of light: crops/dusk_pulse.png renders the same Pulse layout, the same six feeling objects in the same order and with the same timestamps (empty chair 17:19, ugh 16:58, confetti 16:23, hold 11:54, nyeh 06:42, goodnight 21:58) as 01_pulse.png under a warmer key, with no element swapped for a different idiom.

The clips are honest about themselves: frames.json reports 0 repeated frames, 0 brightness jumps and playback_over_app_time 1.042 for all five, and I confirmed the frame counts (256, 314, 395, 300, 304) against ffprobe.

verdict: On the evidence this really is one system rather than an assembly, and the strongest parts of the case are measurable rather than impressionistic: every region report carries the same 14,062 events and the same seed, the ambient partner-state banner is pixel-identical across all seven region stills, one chat stream carries messages, photographs, feelings, Pulse signals and a Us to-do side by side, one search returns nine event types, and the Us region already runs five modules on one {id, events, glance} shape, so the fifth-module question is answered on screen rather than argued. What holds it back is that the one visual language does not survive contact with the edges of the system. Chat and Moments both render events as flat, untextured, straight-edged rectangles beside torn inked paper (06_unfolding carries them in all 256 frames, 246 scanlines at the median; 04_moments leaves eight tiles with nothing in flight to fill them), a millisecond-numbered sensation instrument overprints the composer for 370 of 395 frames of 08 and 280 of 304 of 15, the one signal-divider renderer produces "you is heads down" for the local person and "noor's phone is on normal" for the other, and 17_setup_pwa drops the wood the whole app stands on for a flat ground measuring std 1.8. Above all, the clause of this row that names both platforms has nothing behind it: every artifact was captured under webkit, frames.json says no Android device was up, and the two artifacts that exist to show the second phone are absent with a reason that only restates the absence. I have marked that blocking, and I want to be precise about why — not because a defect was demonstrated, but because half of what this row asks me to check was not put in front of me. Nothing else moved this cycle either: fourteen artifacts are byte-identical to the previous capture and the fifteenth is frame-for-frame identical despite its "changed" label, so this report is, by measurement, the same report the last capture would have earned.
